Rice protein in the HMI library has 47 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel and chromium from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Metals in Selected Foods  to  April 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019: Food chemistry  to  Targeted surveys  to  Final report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Food Inspection Agency</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfia2020-toxic-metals-selected-foods-2018-19">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Lopez-Calabozo and colleagues reported lead at 175 µg/kg (mean ± 3.15 SD) in rice protein, as sold from Rice protein concentrate, anonymized product 2.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the rice protein came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. The EU sets a maximum of 1,000 µg/kg cadmium for food supplements (as placed on the market; this is the supplement row, not a rice-protein row).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-rice-protein" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-rice-protein-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of rice protein, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach rice protein

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

No study in the library compared rice protein from contaminated and ordinary settings, so the routes by which metals reach it are not measured here.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

The HMI reference for total arsenic in rice protein, as sold pools 15 subgroup units from 1 sampling family, with a median of 100 µg/kg and a middle half spanning 86 (lower quartile) and 120 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, the 2013 release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic in rice protein, as sold, the reference median was 45.5 µg/kg, with a middle half from 38 to 69 µg/kg across 16 units.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, the 2013 release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, total arsenic across 13 groups of rice protein ranged from 82 µg/kg (Protein beverage product labeled rice or brown rice protein) to 230 µg/kg (Dietary supplement, rice protein powders, sample 334093956); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, the 2013 release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>


<a id="processing-cooking-and-preparation"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

No study in the library measured the same rice protein before and after washing, peeling, drying or cooking for metals, so no processing effect can be stated. Heat does not destroy metals; cooking or drying changes a concentration by moving water or metal, not by removing the element.


<a id="mitigation-for-rice-protein"></a>
<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for rice protein

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

No control for metals in rice protein was measured in the library; lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable step.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No study in this library has yet measured a way to lower heavy metals in rice protein; the results above show the levels measured, and lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable check.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of rice protein measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, total arsenic across 13 groups of rice protein ranged from 82 µg/kg (Protein beverage product labeled rice or brown rice protein) to 230 µg/kg (Dietary supplement, rice protein powders, sample 334093956); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, the 2013 release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in rice protein is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 19 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, the 2013 release</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## What remains uncertain

Growing origin is not reported for these lots, so a country ranking is not supported. Where arsenic species were marked not speciated, the printed inorganic arsenic cell is held out of the reference. A trace result sits between the detection limit and the quantification limit. The single brown rice protein mercury result is one sample, and the survey means for all protein powders mix protein sources. A rice endosperm protein trial and a Hungarian retail survey are named in the deposit notes, but their tables are not in this unit, so their numbers are not used. No study here measured a before-and-after reduction of metals in rice protein.
